titulo: Modals - must/can’t deduction / Modals – might, may
titulo_es: Modals of deduction in the present (must, might, could, can't)
descripcion_es: Expressing certainty, possibility or impossibility about the present based on evidence.
resumen: Must, might, may, could and can't + infinitive are used to deduce something about the present depending on how sure we are: almost certainly yes, maybe, almost certainly not.

filas: The lights are on. They must be at home.
She might be in a meeting.
He may not know the address.
That can't be Juan. He's in Peru.

explicacion.texto: The opposite of must (deduction) is can't, not mustn't. Mustn't expresses prohibition: You mustn't smoke here. To say “it's impossible” you use can't: It can't be true.

items: The modal is followed by the infinitive without to: She must be tired (not must to be).
For something happening now: modal + be + -ing: They must be sleeping.
Could not (couldn't) also expresses impossibility, but in the positive could expresses possibility, not certainty.
Approximate equivalents in Spanish: must be = “debe de ser”; can't be = “no puede ser”; might be = “a lo mejor es”.

ejemplos.frase: You've been walking all day. You must be exhausted.
ejemplos.traduccion: Llevas todo el día andando. Debes de estar agotado.

ejemplos.frase: Someone is at the door. It might be the postman.
ejemplos.traduccion: Hay alguien en la puerta. A lo mejor es el cartero.

ejemplos.frase: This bill can't be right. We only had two coffees.
ejemplos.traduccion: Esta cuenta no puede estar bien. Solo tomamos dos cafés.

ejemplos.frase: Her phone is off. She may be on a plane.
ejemplos.traduccion: Tiene el móvil apagado. Puede que esté en un avión.

ejemplos.frase: They aren't answering. They must be having dinner.
ejemplos.traduccion: No contestan. Deben de estar cenando.

ejemplos.frase: Take an umbrella; it could rain later.
ejemplos.traduccion: Llévate un paraguas; podría llover más tarde.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: He mustn't be at home; his car isn't here.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: He can't be at home; his car isn't here.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: For a negative deduction use can't; mustn't expresses prohibition.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: She must to be very rich.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Modals are followed by the infinitive without to.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: She must be in the office, but I'm not sure.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: She might be in the office, but I'm not sure.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: If it is only a possibility, use might/may/could; must expresses near certainty.

ejercicios.frase: He's been working for twelve hours. He ___ be tired.
ejercicios.explicacion: The first row of the table applies: almost certainly yes = must. The clue is the evidence: he has been working for twelve hours, from which we draw an almost certain conclusion. It is followed by the infinitive without to: must be tired.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Almost certain deduction from evidence: must.
ejercicios.traduccion: Lleva doce horas trabajando. Debe de estar cansado.

por_opcion.must: Correct: almost certain deduction from clear evidence.
por_opcion.can't: Incorrect: it would say that it is impossible that he is tired, the opposite of what the evidence suggests.
por_opcion.mustn't: Incorrect: mustn't expresses prohibition (he is not allowed to), not deduction.

ejercicios.frase: That ___ be Laura's car. She sold it last year.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives can't for almost certainly not. The clue is She sold it last year: we have a clear reason to rule it out. The sheet reminds you that the opposite of must is can't, not mustn't.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ese no puede ser el coche de Laura. Lo vendió el año pasado.

por_opcion.must: Incorrect: it would state that it is her car, when we know she sold it.
por_opcion.might: Incorrect: it would leave the possibility open, but the fact rules it out almost certainly.
por_opcion.can't: Correct: impossibility deduced from a clear fact.

ejercicios.frase: I'm not sure where Pablo is. He ___ be in the library.
ejercicios.explicacion: The row for possible in the table is might / may / could. The clue is I'm not sure: we are not certain, we only have a hypothesis. So He might be in the library.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: It is only a possibility: might.
ejercicios.traduccion: No sé dónde está Pablo. A lo mejor está en la biblioteca.

por_opcion.must: Incorrect: it expresses near certainty, which is incompatible with I'm not sure.
por_opcion.can't: Incorrect: it would rule out the library, when the sentence suggests it as an option.

ejercicios.frase: Listen to that noise! The neighbours ___ having a party.
ejercicios.explicacion: The list in the sheet says that for something happening now you use modal + be + -ing. The clue is having, in -ing, which needs be before it. So must be having, an almost certain deduction from the noise.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¡Escucha ese ruido! Los vecinos deben de estar de fiesta.

por_opcion.must be: Correct: must + be + having for an action in progress.
por_opcion.must: Incorrect: must having is not grammatical; be is missing.
por_opcion.can't: Incorrect: as well as be being missing, can't contradicts the evidence of the noise.

ejercicios.frase: You ___ be serious! That's a terrible idea.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule of can't for “it's impossible” applies: here it expresses disbelief. The clue is the reaction That's a terrible idea, which shows that the speaker doesn't believe the other person is being serious. The full form cannot is also accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¡No puedes estar hablando en serio! Es una idea malísima.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Mustn't expresses prohibition; for “it's impossible” you use can't.
You must be serious would say that he is surely being serious, the opposite of the disbelief in the context.

ejercicios.frase: The restaurant is always full. The food ___ be very good.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives must for an almost certain positive deduction. The clue is the evidence: it is always full. From that we conclude that the food is good: must be very good.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Clear evidence leading to a positive conclusion: must.
ejercicios.traduccion: El restaurante siempre está lleno. La comida debe de ser muy buena.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Can't would say that it is impossible that it is good, contrary to the evidence.
The modal is not followed by to: must be.

ejercicios.frase: She ___ be hungry. She's just eaten a huge sandwich.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule of can't for almost certainly not applies. The clue is She's just eaten a huge sandwich, a clear reason to rule out that she is hungry. Cannot is also accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: No puede tener hambre. Acaba de comerse un bocadillo enorme.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Mustn't expresses prohibition (she is not allowed to be hungry); for deduction you use can't.
Must would say that she is surely hungry, the opposite of what the sandwich suggests.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the negative form of might.
ejercicios.frase: Call him before you go. He ___ be at home this afternoon.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives might not / may not for possibly not. The clue is Call him before you go: the advice makes sense because there is a possibility that he isn't there. The instruction asks for the negative of might, so might not or the contraction mightn't.
ejercicios.traduccion: Llámale antes de ir. Puede que no esté en casa esta tarde.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Can't would state that he is almost certainly not there; here it is only a possibility.
Mustn't is prohibition, not possibility.
Not goes after the modal: might not.

ejercicios.frase: It mustn't be Tom on the phone; he never calls at this time.
respuestas: It can't be Tom on the phone; he never calls at this time.
ejercicios.explicacion: The sheet stresses that negative deduction is made with can't, not with mustn't, which expresses prohibition. The clue is he never calls at this time, a reason to rule it out almost certainly. You just need to change mustn't to can't.
ejercicios.traduccion: No puede ser Tom el que llama; nunca llama a estas horas.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It mustn't be Tom on the phone; he never calls at this time.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: mustn't cannot be used for deduction.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It doesn't must be Tom on the phone; he never calls at this time.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Modals don't take do; besides, negative deduction is can't.

ejercicios.explicacion: The list in the sheet reminds you that the modal is followed by the infinitive without to. Might, like all modals, is followed directly by the verb: might be lost. Ought to and have to are not pure modals and that is why they cause confusion.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: might is not followed by to.
After the modal the verb is in the base form: be, not are.

ejercicios.explicacion: The sheet equates I'm sure + affirmative statement with must. The verb is becomes the infinitive without to (be) after the modal, and I'm sure disappears because must already expresses the certainty.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After must comes the base form: be.
No to after the modal.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'm sure she must be Italian.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is redundant: must already expresses the certainty of I'm sure.

ejercicios.explicacion: The sheet equates I'm sure + negative with can't. The sentence I'm sure it isn't true becomes It can't be true, with be as an infinitive without to. Cannot is also accepted.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Mustn't expresses prohibition; negative deduction is can't.
After can't comes the base form: be.

ejercicios.frase: Perhaps they are in the garden.
respuestas: They might be in the garden.
ejercicios.explicacion: The sheet equates perhaps with might to express possibility. The verb are becomes be after might, and perhaps disappears because might already expresses it. There is no clue of certainty, so must would not work.
ejercicios.traduccion: A lo mejor están en el jardín.

errores_previstos.respuesta: They might are in the garden.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After might comes the base form: be.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Perhaps they might be in the garden.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Perhaps and might say the same thing; the transformation asks you to replace one with the other.

errores_previstos.respuesta: They must be in the garden.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Must expresses near certainty; perhaps only expresses possibility.

ejercicios.explicacion: The list in the sheet gives modal + be + -ing for something happening now. You must be joking is a very common expression to show surprise or disbelief. The order is subject, must, be and the verb in -ing.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Modal + be + -ing for something happening now.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The modal goes before be: must be.
That order makes a question; the expression is affirmative: you must be joking.

descripcion_larga_es: The modals must, might, may, could and can't followed by an infinitive are used to deduce something about the present depending on how sure we are: almost certainly yes, maybe or almost certainly not. It is a very common tool in speech, and it is hard for Spanish speakers because Spanish “no debe de ser” is not translated as mustn't, which expresses prohibition in English, but as can't.

contexto.que_es: It is the use of some modal verbs to express a logical conclusion about the present: must (near certainty), might, may and could (possibility), might not and may not (negative possibility) and can't (negative near certainty). They are followed by the infinitive without to, or by be + -ing if the action is in progress.
contexto.por_que_importa: They are used every day to interpret what we see or hear: It must be the postman, You must be tired. Confusing can't with mustn't changes the message (prohibiting versus deducing), and using must instead of might shows a certainty you don't have. In B1 exams it appears in gap-fills and in transformations with I'm sure and perhaps.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When there is evidence (the lights are on, there is noise, the restaurant is always full) and we want to draw a conclusion about the present. The signals are expressions such as I'm sure, perhaps, I'm not sure. Spanish speakers tend to translate “no debe de” as mustn't and to put to after the modal.
